critical_code_review_comments: server.py:184-245 in-memory brute-force limiter is correctly implemented (per-IP + per-employee-id fixed-window, dummy bcrypt on unknown IDs to hide timing enumeration, 429 with Retry-After header). NOTE: state is per-process and lost on restart or with multiple workers/pods behind a load balancer; if the app is ever scaled horizontally, move counters to Redis to keep limits enforceable.

server.py:220-222 IP resolution trusts the first token of X-Forwarded-For unconditionally. In a public deployment behind a trusted proxy this is fine, but if the ingress ever fronts an untrusted network, per-IP blocks can be trivially bypassed by rotating X-Forwarded-For. Consider pinning to the right-most trusted proxy hop.

server.py:657 salesperson-collection ownership check treats retailer.salesperson_id=None as 'anyone can collect'. This is intentional per the review note but means admin-created retailers can be collected on by any salesperson until reassigned. If that's undesirable, either force salesperson_id at retailer-creation time or 403 when it's None for salesperson role.

server.py:713-721 file download only checks upload record's owner_id vs current user; there is no additional check that the record path prefix contains user id. Records inserted by the app always use path=APP_NAME/uploads/<user_id>/<uuid>.<ext> so it matches, but if any legacy row has mismatched owner_id vs path components it could be exploitable. Consider verifying path.startswith(f"{APP_NAME}/uploads/{owner_id}/") at upload time.
server.py:190 DUMMY_HASH is computed at module import with bcrypt.gensalt(); this is fine but takes ~200ms on cold start and blocks the event loop briefly. Acceptable trade-off.
backend/.env now contains a rotated 64-char hex JWT_SECRET; all previously issued tokens are invalidated as expected. Confirmed clients must re-login.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration-4 file /app/backend/tests/test_iteration4_security.py runs in ~7s with xdist (2 workers) via /app/backend/pytest.ini. IMPORTANT: TestZZZBruteForce triggers the in-memory limiter on the client IP for ~5 minutes; the test suite already restarts backend after (via the 429 header check + suite-end), but if you re-run tests within 5 minutes and see 429s during login, execute `sudo supervisorctl restart backend` to clear the block. The suite uses class-name alphabetical ordering (zzz_) to guarantee brute-force runs last. pymongo direct write is used ONCE (in emp5_retailer fixture) because there is no admin endpoint to reassign a retailer's salesperson_id — if such an endpoint is added later, switch to it. All other testIDs and flows from iter-1..3 are still valid. login-employee-id-input / login-password-input / login-submit-button remain the correct login testIDs. JWT secret is stable at commit time; if it is rotated again, all existing tokens (including any cached in the frontend AsyncStorage) will invalidate and the frontend will need to log in fresh (expected behavior).
rca_of_issue: No blocking bugs. All 8 security fixes verified. Non-blocking observations: (a) in-memory rate limiter won't survive multi-pod scale-out (needs Redis if ever horizontally scaled), (b) X-Forwarded-For is trusted unconditionally so a rogue upstream could bypass IP-block, (c) retailer.salesperson_id=None is intentionally treated as unassigned/any-sp for collection ownership — behaviour is by design but worth documenting.
